title: COEX in Gangnam: Seoul's Underground Mall With a Library, Aquarium, and More (Beginner's Guide)
html:
If someone tells you to meet them "at COEX" in Seoul, don't picture a single building — picture an entire underground world. COEX (short for "COnvention centers" and "EXhibition halls") is a huge complex in Gangnam that mixes a trade convention center with one of the world's largest underground shopping malls, a famous library, an aquarium, a cinema, a hotel, and a department store — all connected so you barely have to step outside. For first-time visitors, it's an easy, weatherproof way to spend half a day (or more) without planning much at all. Here's what's actually inside, what's worth your time, and how to get there without getting lost.

What Is COEX, Exactly?

Photo: COEX complex, Gangnam, Seoul, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

COEX opened in 1988 as a business and trade center, run by the Korea International Trade Association (KITA). On the surface, it's still a working convention center — trade shows, expos, and business conferences happen here year-round. But underneath and around it is Starfield COEX Mall, which most travelers mean when they just say "COEX." The whole site also connects to a department store, Korea's largest convention-area hotel, and a subway station, so locals and tourists alike use it as a single giant indoor destination rather than separate buildings.

Starfield Library: The Photo Everyone Takes

Photo: Inside COEX, Gangnam, Seoul, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

Right in the middle of the mall sits Starfield Library (별마당도서관, "Byeolmadang Library"), a public reading space with bookshelves that reach about 13 meters (43 feet) high. It's become one of the most photographed indoor spots in Seoul — you'll see people lining up just to take a picture from the escalator above it. The good news for budget-conscious travelers: it's free to enter, with no ticket or reservation needed. It's generally open from mid-morning until around 10 PM daily, but hours can shift slightly around holidays or events, so it's worth a quick check on the day if you're planning around it. You can sit, read (some books are in English), or just admire the shelves — just know that weekday evenings and weekends tend to get crowded with people doing the same thing you are.

COEX Aquarium: Korea's Biggest

Photo: Inside COEX, Gangnam, Seoul, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

A few minutes' walk from the library is COEX Aquarium, home to roughly 40,000 marine animals across more than 600 species, making it one of the largest aquariums in the country. It's a solid rainy-day or hot-summer pick, especially if you're traveling with kids. Unlike the library, this one isn't free — admission typically runs somewhere in the $15–22 USD range depending on where you buy it, and tickets booked online in advance (through sites like Klook) are usually a bit cheaper than paying at the door. It's generally open from around 10 AM to 8 PM, with the last entry about an hour before closing — but since hours and prices do change, double-check the official listing for your travel dates before you go.

Shopping, SM Town, and a Food Court for Every Craving

Photo: Inside COEX Mall, Gangnam, Seoul, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

Beyond the library and aquarium, the mall itself has hundreds of shops, a Megabox movie theater, and a Hyundai Department Store attached to one side. K-pop fans will want to look for SM Town, a themed store and exhibition space tied to SM Entertainment, tucked near the COEX Artium theater (if you want more on that theater specifically, we've covered it in a separate guide). There's also a large basement food court with everything from Korean street food to international chains — it's the kind of place where locals actually grab a quick lunch between meetings or errands, not just a tourist stop, so don't expect it to feel empty or "touristy." Because COEX is enormous and partly underground, it's genuinely easy to get turned around — use the directory screens near the escalators, or just ask any staff member for the section you're looking for.

Getting to COEX: Subway Directions

Photo: Entrance area at COEX, Gangnam, Seoul, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

The address is 513 Yeongdong-daero, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, and you don't need a car:

  • Samseong Station (Line 2), Exits 5 or 6 — the main route most visitors use, leading straight into an underground passage toward the mall.
  • Bongeunsa Station (Line 9), Exit 7 — connects through ASEM Plaza, a good option if you're coming from western Seoul. Bongeunsa Station is named after the historic Bongeunsa Temple, which sits right next to COEX and is free to walk into if you want a quiet, traditional contrast to the mall.
  • Cheongdam Station (Line 7), Exit 2 — also connects, but it's a longer walk (10+ minutes).

One thing that surprises a lot of first-timers: in heavy rain, summer heat, or winter cold, locals will often walk several subway stops out of their way through these underground tunnels just to avoid going outside at all. It's a very "Seoul" habit, and COEX is one of the best places to try it yourself.

Tips for First-Time Visitors

Photo: Inside COEX, Gangnam, Seoul, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

  • Give yourself at least 3–4 hours if you want to see the library, aquarium, and do some shopping — it's bigger than it looks on a map.
  • Weekday mornings are calmest. Weekends and evenings bring crowds, especially around Starfield Library.
  • Buy aquarium tickets online beforehand if you can — it saves time standing in line and is usually a little cheaper.
  • Bring your T-money card for the subway, and remember your T-money also works for small purchases at convenience stores inside the mall.
  • Pair it with Bongeunsa Temple next door for a half-day that mixes modern mall culture with a 1,200-year-old Buddhist temple — a nice contrast for a first trip to Korea.

💬 Planning a stop at COEX, or curious about the library, the aquarium, or how to get there? Drop your question in the comments below — happy to help!
meta_description: A first-timer's guide to COEX in Gangnam: Starfield Library, the aquarium, shopping, and food court, plus how to get there by subway.
